---
title: "SpaRTaCo benchmarking (parallel)"
output: html_document
---

<!--
  Parallel variant of SpaRTaCo.Rmd. The independent slides run concurrently
  (one worker per slide) instead of serially.

  IMPORTANT -- why this uses a PSOCK cluster, NOT mclapply (fork), unlike
  BISON_parallel.Rmd:

    spartaco::spartaco() parallelises ITSELF internally. It ships its own
    mclapply2(), which opens a fifo(tempfile()), forks a progress-monitor
    process (parallel:::mcfork()), and shuttles data with readBin/writeBin
    while drawing a txtProgressBar. If we wrap spartaco() inside our own
    fork-based mclapply(), we get NESTED forking: N outer fork-workers each
    running spartaco's inner fork+fifo machinery, all sharing inherited file
    descriptors and the same stdout. The progress/verbose streams interleave
    and corrupt each other -> "Error in rawToChar(bytes): embedded nul in
    string" -> dead workers -> the whole (multi-hour) run dies at the final
    bind_rows. (BISON has no such internal parallelism, so fork is fine there.)

    A PSOCK cluster gives each slide its OWN independent R process (separate
    tempdir, fifos, stdout, and HDF5 dump dir), so spartaco runs exactly as it
    does in a clean serial session -- which works. We also pass verbose = FALSE
    and cap spartaco's internal cores per worker to keep total load in check.

  Other notes:
   * calculate_stats() appends to a shared stats.csv (read -> rbind -> write),
     which is NOT safe under parallelism. Each worker instead RETURNS its stats
     row (read-only calculate_ARI/calculate_F1) and we write stats.csv ONCE at
     the end, merging by model so BISON's rows are preserved.
   * plot_annotations()/save_annotations() write unique per-slide paths inside
     the worker -> parallel-safe.
   * Nothing in models/ is modified. benchmarking_scripts_2.R and constants.R
     are sourced unchanged (on both master and workers).
-->

```{r}
## Install SpaRTaCo once (skip if already present -- avoids a network hit and a
## rebuild on every knit).
if (!requireNamespace("spartaco", quietly = TRUE)) {
  remotes::install_github("andreasottosanti/spartaco", build_vignettes = TRUE)
}
```

```{r}
library(parallel)

## Master only needs the dataset -> slide grid to build the job list; the heavy
## libraries and helpers are loaded on the workers.
source("constants.R")
proj_dir <- getwd()

model <- "SpaRTaCo"

datasets <- list(
  "DLPFC" = DLPFC_files,
  "HER2+" = HER2_files,
  "MOSTA" = MOSTA_files
  # "Mouse hypothalamus" = mouse_hypothalamus_files
)
```

```{r}
## Flatten the (dataset, slide) grid into a list of independent jobs.
jobs <- list()
for (dataset_name in names(datasets)) {
  for (file in names(datasets[[dataset_name]])) {
    jobs[[length(jobs) + 1]] <- list(dataset_name = dataset_name, file = file)
  }
}

## PSOCK sizing + BLAS thread cap.
##
## spartaco's heavy work is multithreaded OpenBLAS linear algebra. Left uncapped,
## EACH worker process spawns one BLAS thread per core (~56 here), so a handful
## of workers push the load average to 200+ on a 56-core box -- catastrophic
## thrashing that makes the run far slower (not an error, just self-sabotage).
##
## Fix: cap BLAS threads per worker so n_workers * blas_per stays under the core
## count. OpenBLAS reads OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS/OMP_NUM_THREADS at process startup;
## PSOCK workers inherit them from this master, which inherits them from the
## shell that launched R. So set them at launch, e.g.:
##     OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=4 OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::render(...)'
## (RhpcBLASctl, which could set this at runtime, isn't installed here.)
avail     <- max(1L, detectCores() - 2L)
blas_per  <- max(1L, as.integer(Sys.getenv("OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS", unset = "1")))
n_workers <- min(length(jobs), max(1L, avail %/% blas_per))
message(sprintf("SpaRTaCo parallel: %d workers x %d BLAS threads = %d cores (of %d)",
                n_workers, blas_per, n_workers * blas_per, detectCores()))

## Runs one slide end-to-end and RETURNS its stats row (no shared writes here).
## Runs on a PSOCK worker; it resolves model/loaders/assay_names and the helper
## functions from the worker's global env (populated by clusterEvalQ below).
run_one <- function(job) {
  dataset_name <- job$dataset_name
  file         <- job$file

  loader     <- loaders[[dataset_name]]
  assay_name <- assay_names[[dataset_name]]

  tryCatch({
    loaded     <- loader(file)
    sce        <- preprocess_data(loaded$sce, file)
    n_clusters <- loaded$n_clusters

    res <- run_spartaco(
      sce,
      level       = n_clusters,
      sample_name = file,
      assay_name  = assay_name,
      K           = 10,          # tune independently of n_clusters
      verbose     = FALSE,       # silence spartaco's progress fifo/mcfork
      export_path = file.path(
        "annotation_results", model,
        sprintf("%s_%s_annotations.csv", dataset_name, file)
      )
    )

    plot_annotations(
      res$sce,
      model = model, level = n_clusters, predicted = res$predicted_key,
      tissue = dataset_name, slide = file,
      export_path = file.path("figures", "spatial", model,
                              sprintf("%s_%s_predicted_plot.png", dataset_name, file))
    )

    ari <- calculate_ARI(res$sce, res$predicted_key)
    f1  <- calculate_F1(res$sce, res$predicted_key)

    data.frame(
      Model = model, Dataset = dataset_name, Slide = file,
      ARI = ari, F1_Weighted = f1$f1_weighted, F1_Score = f1$f1_macro
    )
  }, error = function(e) {
    # Don't let one bad slide kill the whole run; surface it in the results.
    data.frame(
      Model = model, Dataset = dataset_name, Slide = file,
      ARI = NA_real_, F1_Weighted = NA_real_, F1_Score = NA_real_,
      error = conditionMessage(e)
    )
  })
}

cl <- makeCluster(n_workers, type = "PSOCK")

## NB: do NOT use on.exit(stopCluster(cl)) here. knitr evaluates chunk code
## outside a function, so an on.exit() fires almost immediately and tears the
## cluster down BEFORE we use it -> clusterExport hits "invalid connection".
## Use tryCatch(..., finally=) so the cluster is still cleaned up on error.
rows <- tryCatch({
  ## Each worker is an independent process: set the project wd (loaders use
  ## relative paths), bound spartaco's internal fork width, load libraries,
  ## source the (unchanged) helpers, and define the per-model config it looks up.
  clusterExport(cl, c("proj_dir", "blas_per"), envir = environment())
  clusterEvalQ(cl, {
    setwd(proj_dir)
    ## Belt-and-suspenders: also set the BLAS caps inside the worker (they were
    ## already inherited from the master's env at spawn; this is a no-op if so).
    Sys.setenv(OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS = blas_per, OMP_NUM_THREADS = blas_per)
    if (requireNamespace("RhpcBLASctl", quietly = TRUE)) {
      RhpcBLASctl::blas_set_num_threads(blas_per)
      RhpcBLASctl::omp_set_num_threads(blas_per)
    }
    options(mc.cores = 1L)   # spartaco parallelism comes from BLAS threads, not forks
    suppressMessages({
      library(spartaco)
      library(SingleCellExperiment)
      library(HDF5Array)
    })
    source("benchmarking_scripts_2.R")
    source("constants.R")
    model <- "SpaRTaCo"
    loaders <- list(
      "DLPFC" = load_DLPFC,
      "HER2+" = load_HER2,
      "MOSTA" = load_MOSTA
    )
    assay_names <- list(
      "DLPFC" = "counts",
      "HER2+" = "counts",
      "MOSTA" = "count"   # load_MOSTA exposes the raw layer as both "count" and "counts"
    )
    NULL
  })
  parLapply(cl, jobs, run_one)
}, finally = {
  stopCluster(cl)
})
```

```{r}
## Defensive: if any worker returned a non-data.frame (e.g. a hard crash),
## coerce it into an error row so it can't sink the whole run's output.
rows <- Map(function(r, job) {
  if (is.data.frame(r)) return(r)
  data.frame(
    Model = model, Dataset = job$dataset_name, Slide = job$file,
    ARI = NA_real_, F1_Weighted = NA_real_, F1_Score = NA_real_,
    error = paste("worker returned non-data.frame:",
                  paste(utils::head(as.character(r), 3), collapse = " | "))
  )
}, rows, jobs)

new_stats <- dplyr::bind_rows(rows)  # tolerates the optional `error` column

## Merge into stats.csv WITHOUT clobbering other models' rows: drop any existing
## SpaRTaCo rows (so re-runs replace rather than duplicate), keep everything else
## (e.g. BISON), then append this run. Written exactly once.
if (file.exists("stats.csv")) {
  existing <- read.csv("stats.csv", check.names = FALSE)
  existing <- existing[existing$Model != model, , drop = FALSE]
  stats <- dplyr::bind_rows(existing, new_stats)
} else {
  stats <- new_stats
}

print(new_stats)
write.csv(stats, "stats.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```
